quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
questions.explanation: You must stop for blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog. Always let them cross safely before you continue.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent will:

options.text: Not affect your driving at all.
Not put other drivers at risk.
Double your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Double your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles your risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: What is a distraction while driving?

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can cause crashes that result in damage, injury, or death.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat, mirrors, and seatbelt before moving your vehicle. Never adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes during a skid. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning when the road is wet?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep your speed steady.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down on wet pavement to prevent it.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the immediate left of the cab.
Both directly behind the truck and on the immediate left of the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both directly behind the truck and on the immediate left of the cab.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots behind them and on the left side. If you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: When following a large truck on the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: Close behind it in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Farther behind than you would a regular car.
No more than one car length back so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind than you would a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too close, the truck driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Tailgating removes your safety cushion if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: You reach a four-way stop intersection at the same time as the driver to your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You do.
Whoever signals a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You do.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at a four-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a school crossing sign?

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A school crossing sign warns you are near a school zone. Be alert and prepared to stop.

questions.question: In rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. They help other drivers see you, even if they don't help you see much better.

questions.question: Vehicles behind a school bus with red flashing lights must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students get off the bus.
The stop arm is pulled in.
The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving again.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving again.
questions.explanation: Stop completely when a school bus flashes red lights and extends its stop arm. Stay stopped until the lights turn off, the arm retracts, and the bus moves again.

questions.question: At a flashing red light, you should:

options.text: Slow down and let others go first.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, let others pass, and then go when safe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings show a pedestrian crossing. Watch for pedestrians and let them cross safely.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: Children do not have adult reflexes.
Children are smaller and harder to see.
Both reasons above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both reasons above.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, and parks. Children on bikes may suddenly enter the road.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line is next to a broken yellow line, passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Let pedestrians cross safely in any marked or unmarked crosswalk. For safety, yield to people crossing any street.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights until you are 10 feet away.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when following another vehicle. Only use high beams in rural areas when no other cars are nearby.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up and merge smoothly with interstate traffic. Do not stop like you would on other roads.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from the side next to the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed only from the side next to the dashed line.
questions.explanation: Only drivers next to the dashed line can pass. Drivers next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car or other property, you must leave a note attached to it. Include your name, phone number, and address.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?

options.text: Only when leaving the curb.
When approaching the curb, but not when leaving it.
When approaching or leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When approaching or leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal both when parking next to a curb and when leaving it.

questions.question: A pedestrian is using a guide dog or white cane. What must you do?

options.text: Always give them the right-of-way.
Tell them where to cross the street.
Only give them the right-of-way at corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give them the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: You must always yield the right-of-way to blind or partially blind pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: You are stopped at a red light with a green arrow. When may you turn in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes.
If you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You may turn in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane. The intersection must be clear of pedestrians and other vehicles.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
As you drive faster, you should increase your following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds greatly increase the risk of death in a crash. Faster speeds also require longer stopping distances, so you need more space between your car and the car ahead.

questions.question: You are in a turn lane to make a left turn. There is oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left to prepare to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Start signaling about 100 feet before the turn. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if a car hits you from behind.

questions.question: You need to park in an unusual spot. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your car from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your car from all directions.
questions.explanation: Your parked car should not become a hazard. Make sure it is visible to drivers coming from any direction.

questions.question: Oncoming cars are on your left. Parked cars are on your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming cars than the parked cars.
Closer to the parked cars than the oncoming cars.
Right in the middle between both.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right in the middle between both.
questions.explanation: Steer in the middle between the oncoming cars and parked cars.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection. An emergency vehicle is approaching with its siren and lights on. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection.
Pull to the right and stop.
Finish crossing the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in the intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches, continue across and then drive to the right and stop. Always yield to emergency vehicles.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When there is not enough room on the other side to completely clear the tracks.
When the crossing is in a town with frequent trains.
When you have young children in the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is not enough room on the other side to completely clear the tracks.
questions.explanation: Trains can come at any time on any track. Make sure your car completely clears the tracks before you stop.

questions.question: You see orange construction signs and cones on the freeway. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down because a lane ends ahead.
Prepare for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Construction signs warn you about workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You are leaving an alley or driveway to enter traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop before entering the sidewalk. Pedestrians and traffic already on the road have the right-of-way.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means:

options.text: Both directions can pass.
The vehicle next to the broken line can pass.
The vehicle next to the solid line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle next to the broken line can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, how fast should you drive?

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going over the legal speed limit.

questions.question: From top to bottom, what is the correct order of colors on a traffic light?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to traffic signals ahead.

questions.question: What does this stop sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before the intersection where you can see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A school bus ahead on your side has red lights flashing. What must you do?

options.text: Slow to 10 mph or less.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and wait until the lights stop flashing. Never pass a bus loading or unloading students.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
The driver who arrived first.
The driver across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrived first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles should go in the order they arrive. If multiple vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: To merge into highway traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Watch only the cars behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the car ahead.
Speed up and make other cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Always check for traffic behind and to the side before changing lanes.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: Neither lane can pass.
Both lanes can pass.
The right lane can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane can pass.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.
